road.title: Where you went
road.place: The Windy Ledge of the Seventh Draft
road.description: A thin, anxious presence in a uniform that belongs to a different job, sitting on a trunk they will not discuss. Perpetua is a Returned Explorer and went somewhere once, came back, and has measured everyone else's trips against it ever since.

road.description: A thin, anxious presence in a uniform that belongs to a different job, sitting on a trunk they will not discuss. Perpetua is a Returned Explorer and went somewhere once, came back, and has measured everyone else's trips against it ever since.

openObjectives.prompt: Perpetua has a map with pins in it and is holding one more pin. Tell Perpetua where you went yesterday or last week, using Italian.
Perpetua keeps a book of departures, and you are not in it. Tell Perpetua when you left, using Italian.
Tell Perpetua who you went with, or that you went alone, using Italian.

character.name: Perpetua Clodpole
character.description: A thin, anxious presence in a uniform that belongs to a different job, sitting on a trunk they will not discuss. Perpetua is a Returned Explorer and went somewhere once, came back, and has measured everyone else's trips against it ever since.

npc.narrative: You climb onto the ledge, where the vento arrives from seven directions and the notte is full of stelle. Perpetua waves from a piccolo tavolo with una sedia, as if you were a nave coming in. Beside it, a cartello says aperto in letters that have clearly been waiting.
npc.native: Buonasera! Finalmente qualcuno! Uno: una volta sono andata molto lontano. Due: sono partita la mattina e sono tornata la sera. Tre: sto risparmiando per un cappello. E tu, dove sei andato ieri?
npc.translation: Good evening! Finally, someone! One: once I went very far. Two: I left in the morning and came back in the evening. Three: I am saving up for a hat. And you, where did you go yesterday?

player: Buonasera! Ieri sono andato al mare. Era bello!

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely start! You told Perpetua that you went to the sea yesterday and added that it was nice, all in correct Italian.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done: you said where you went yesterday, using "sono andato" correctly.
You haven't said when you left yet. Tell Perpetua what time or day you set off, and she will ask again later.
You haven't said who you went with, or that you went alone. Perpetua will ask for this again later.

openObjectives.prompt: Perpetua keeps a book of departures, and you are not in it. Tell Perpetua when you left, using Italian.
Tell Perpetua who you went with, or that you went alone, using Italian.

npc.narrative: The stelle are out, and Perpetua has set a lanterna on the banco, in case la notte needs serving. She shakes a piccola scatola marked CAPPELLO, which says more than it rattles.
npc.native: Che fortuna, il mare! Io sono partita alle sei, ma il mio viaggio è stato più lungo. Il fondo per il cappello cresce piano. E tu, a che ora sei partito ieri?
npc.translation: What luck, the sea! I left at six, but my journey was longer. The fund for the hat is growing slowly. And you, what time did you leave yesterday?

player: Sono andato con mio fratello. Lui ama nuotare, io no! Sono partito alle otto.

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely answer! You told Perpetua who you went with and when you left, and you added a nice detail about your brother liking to swim.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done: "Sono partito alle otto" tells Perpetua when you left.
Well done: "con mio fratello" says who you went with.

npc.narrative: Under the stelle, Perpetua counts on her dita, as though the cielo owes her a receipt. She holds a small scatola marked cappello, which rattles less than a hat fund should. Near the strada on this quiet notte, a cane waits in the erba, and nobody asks it why.
npc.native: Tuo fratello nuota e tu guardi il mare: è un buon piano. Io sono andata da sola, con un panino. Uno: stasera ci sono molte stelle. Due: il fondo per il cappello è ancora piccolo. Che cosa fai tu al mare, se non nuoti?
npc.translation: Your brother swims and you look at the sea: it is a good plan. I went alone, with a sandwich. One: tonight there are many stars. Two: the fund for the hat is still small. What do you do at the sea, if you don't swim?

player: Leggo un libro e mangio un gelato. E tu, dove sei andata, molto lontano?

npc.narrative: Perpetua leans on her bancone, a plank on two barrels, with the eagerness of someone who has waited all day. Above you the stelle are out in force. Her cane lies in the erba beside the strada, not on it.
npc.native: Sì, molto lontano! Sono andata oltre il ponte vecchio e ho visto tre capre. Uno: la strada era lunga. Due: il cappello costa ancora troppo. Che libro leggi tu?
npc.translation: Yes, very far! I went beyond the old bridge and saw three goats. One: the road was long. Two: the hat still costs too much. What book are you reading?

player: Haha, solo un giorno! Che cappello vuoi? Grande?

npc.narrative: Perpetua shakes a small borsa under the stelle, and it answers with one moneta and a great deal of silenzio. Beside the strada, her cane sits in the erba, facing away, molto calmo.
npc.native: Sì, solo un giorno, ma io ricordo tutto. Il mio cappello è grande, rosso e con una piuma. Uno: costa trenta monete. Due: io ho dieci monete. E tu, porti un cappello al mare?
npc.translation: Yes, only one day, but I remember everything. My hat is big, red and has a feather. One: it costs thirty coins. Two: I have ten coins. And you, do you wear a hat at the seaside?

player: Il mio cappello preferito è rosso. Ma qui c'è troppo vento per un cappello!

npc.narrative: You watch Perpetua hold her collar shut against the vento. Above her, the stelle stay perfectly still, which the wind seems to take personally. She pats her head, where the cappello will one day go, like a woman checking a pocket for a ticket. Un attimo of silence, then she beams.
npc.native: Rosso, come il mio! Hai ragione: stasera c'è molto vento. Uno: il vento non ama i cappelli. Due: i cappelli non amano il vento. E tu, dove metti il cappello quando c'è vento?
npc.translation: Red, like mine! You are right: tonight there is a lot of wind. One: the wind does not love hats. Two: hats do not love the wind. And you, where do you put your hat when there is wind?
